intended_object: The Hodge decomposition of a pure Hodge structure of weight n, viewed as a ℂ-linear isomorphism W ≅ ⊕_p H^{p,n-p} from the complex vector space to the direct sum of its Hodge components. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Deligne, Hodge II §1.2.1).
explanation:
This definition is faithful. It takes the canonical map ⊕_p H^{p,n-p} → W, `DirectSum.coeLinearMap hs.piece`, which sends a family of components to their sum. The theorem `isInternal_piece` proves that this map is bijective, which is the internal direct sum statement of the Hodge decomposition. The definition upgrades the map to a linear equivalence with `LinearEquiv.ofBijective` and inverts it, giving W ≃ₗ[ℂ] ⨁ p, H^{p,n-p}. That is exactly the Hodge decomposition as a linear isomorphism.

The Hodge components are `piece p = F^p ∩ conj(F^{n-p})`, and the rest of the file checks that they behave as expected (`F_eq_iSup_piece`, `conj_piece`).

The generality is right. The setting is a complex vector space with a conjugation (W ⊗ ℂ for a real structure), which is the standard setting for Hodge structures. The definition is just a specialization of the general Mathlib pattern "internal direct sum ⇒ linear equivalence" to the Hodge pieces, so it is not a re-implementation of a more general Mathlib notion. Mathlib has no Hodge-structure counterpart.
